ui.hub.teams.brief.collaboration.note: Names the collaboration brief block inside a disclosed public team row. Small meta weight; one short line.

ui.hub.teams.brief.collaboration_empty.note: The team has no collaboration brief. Same block as a real brief so the row does not reflow.
ui.hub.teams.brief.collaboration_empty.role: fallback sentence where a collaboration brief would be

ui.hub.teams.brief.project.note: Names the project brief block; pairs with brief.collaboration directly above it.

ui.hub.teams.brief.project_empty.note: The team has no project brief. Sits where the pre-line brief text would render.
ui.hub.teams.brief.project_empty.role: fallback sentence where a project brief would be

ui.hub.teams.brief.roster.note: Names the roster list in the disclosed body. Not the same word as the roster heading on the org page if the language distinguishes them.

ui.hub.teams.brief.trigger.note: Visible label of the disclosure that opens a public team's collaboration brief. One short word in English; the accessible name is trigger_aria.
ui.hub.teams.brief.trigger.role: disclosure trigger label on a public team card

ui.hub.teams.brief.trigger_aria.note: Accessible name of the brief disclosure. {name} is the team's display name, never translated. It must keep the visible label 'Brief' recognisable in it (label-in-name).
ui.hub.teams.brief.trigger_aria.role: accessible name for the brief disclosure

ui.hub.teams.brief.unreadable.note: The brief could not be fetched for this one team. The app appends the diagnosis and shows a retry control, so this lead states only what failed.
ui.hub.teams.brief.unreadable.role: failure lead for one team's brief

ui.hub.teams.detail.created.note: {date} arrives already formatted for the reader's locale, so keep it verbatim. The sibling line is detail.updated; the two sit one above the other in the expanded row.
ui.hub.teams.detail.created.role: date line in an expanded team row

ui.hub.teams.detail.updated.note: {date} arrives already formatted for the reader's locale. Pairs with detail.created directly above it.
ui.hub.teams.detail.updated.role: date line in an expanded team row

ui.hub.teams.kind.role.note: A roster slot whose kind is `role` on the wire. The wire token stays English in data; this is only what the roster prints. Narrow cell, never wraps.

ui.hub.teams.kind.specialist.note: A roster slot whose kind is `specialist` on the wire. Sits beside kind.role in the same column, so keep the two comparable in length. Narrow cell.

ui.hub.teams.manager.note: Names the role of the person listed above it in the expanded roster, and is also the row's own caption. One word where the language allows; small meta weight.
ui.hub.teams.manager.role: roster row label under a manager name

ui.hub.teams.manager_label.note: Prefixes the manager's name on the summary row: label, then the name. The colon is part of this message; keep the space handling to the caller.
ui.hub.teams.manager_label.role: inline field label in the composition line

ui.hub.teams.member_count.note: {count} is the number of declared member slots, the manager excluded. ICU plural: the trailing colon belongs to the message. Follow the locale's plural categories, not English's two.
ui.hub.teams.member_count.role: inline count in the composition line

ui.hub.teams.members.note: Title above the roster list inside a disclosed team row. Small meta weight; sentence case in languages that have case.
ui.hub.teams.members.role: section heading in the expanded roster

ui.hub.teams.no_description.note: The team record carries no description, so the summary shows this instead of an empty gap. Must read as a statement, not a call to action.
ui.hub.teams.no_description.role: inline fallback where a description would be

ui.hub.teams.no_members.note: The team declares no member slots. Appears both on the summary line and (only for a row with nothing else) in the expanded body, so it must stand alone in either position.
ui.hub.teams.no_members.role: inline fallback in the composition line and the roster body

ui.hub.teams.org.aria.note: Landmark name of the organization's teams roster. {org} is the organization's name, or the placeholder 'this organization' when the app has no name. Never translate {org}.
ui.hub.teams.org.aria.role: accessible name for the org teams region

ui.hub.teams.org.empty.note: The roster is empty: nothing has been shared into the organization yet. {org} is the organization's name or the placeholder 'this organization'. Says what the roster is for; there is no action to offer here.
ui.hub.teams.org.empty.role: empty-state sentence in the org teams roster

ui.hub.teams.org.load_headline.note: Alert headline for a generic failure to read the org roster. The description under it carries the diagnosis and a retry control.

ui.hub.teams.org.no_access_body.note: {org} is the organization's name or the placeholder 'that organization' (mid-sentence English says 'that', not 'this'). The reader cannot fix this from here, so the sentence names who can.
ui.hub.teams.org.no_access_body.tone: plain, does not blame the reader

ui.hub.teams.org.no_access_headline.note: Alert headline when the backend says the reader is not a member of this organization. Pairs with no_access_body.

ui.hub.teams.org.plan_body.note: {org} is the organization's name or the placeholder 'this organization'. Names the remedy — an owner activates the plan in the Radient console — because the reader may not be the owner. Keep 'Team plan' recognisable as the tier name.

ui.hub.teams.org.plan_headline.note: Alert headline when reading an organization's teams needs the paid Team plan. 'Team plan' is a product tier name, not the team being read.

ui.hub.teams.org.that_organization.note: Placeholder for an organization the app has no name for, used mid-sentence in no_access_body. Lowercase because it follows 'a member of'.

ui.hub.teams.org.unreadable.note: The lead the local backend classifier extends with a diagnosis and a retry, for a generic read failure of the org roster.
ui.hub.teams.org.unreadable.role: failure lead for the org teams roster

ui.hub.teams.public.aria: accessible name and hidden heading for the public library
One name used twice: the region's aria-label and the section's sr-only h2. The h2 keeps the heading outline; the label keeps the landmark.
ui.hub.teams.public.catalogue_unreadable: fallback sentence inside a danger alert
Base sentence handed to the shared public-hub error mapper, which appends the transport detail. 'Public team catalogue' is this surface's name for the read.
ui.hub.teams.public.empty: The public hub carries no teams yet. Says what is missing without a call to action: this surface cannot publish.
ui.hub.teams.public.intro: Explains who publishes these teams, that reading needs no sign-in, and what Pulling does. Three sentences; capped at max-w-3xl and wraps freely.
ui.hub.teams.public.load_failed: The public team read failed as a whole. The explanation and the retry sit beneath it.
ui.hub.teams.public.match_line: status line above the grid while a search is active
{visible} and {total} are counts on this page and its load; {total} takes an ICU plural. {query} is the operator's typed text, escaped and quoted, never translated.
ui.hub.teams.public.open_settings: Opens Settings where the Radient credential is entered. The sentence beside it explains why.
ui.hub.teams.public.published_by: A trailing space is supplied by the caller before the name span; do not bake punctuation into this message that the layout cannot move.

ui.hub.teams.public.pull_failed.note: The public roster's fallback when a pull failed with nothing more specific to say. Rendered under the row's Pull control, beside the control that produced it.

ui.hub.teams.public.pull_no_signin.note: A pull refused because this machine has no Radient sign-in. Points at the settings page rather than a CLI command, because a reader of this window can act on the page. Two sentences: the fact, then the step.

ui.hub.teams.public.search_aria: accessible name for the teams search field
Stable name for the search input; the placeholder beside it is a hint, not a second name.

ui.hub.teams.public.search_miss.note: {query} is what the operator typed, in quotes in English. The sentence is about the teams loaded on THIS page, not the whole hub. A locale may swap the quote pair.
ui.hub.teams.public.search_miss.role: empty search result in the public teams list

ui.hub.teams.public.search_placeholder: placeholder in the teams search field
Placeholder text in the search box above the public teams grid. Fits beside the search icon in an h-8 field.
ui.hub.teams.public.search_scope: inline qualifier after the match line
Leading middle dot and space are part of the message: it is appended to the match sentence as a dim aside. Says search only covers the teams already loaded on this page.
ui.hub.teams.public.sign_in_hint: inline sentence beside the sign-in button
Pulling a team needs a Radient credential on this machine. Radient is a product name and stays English.

ui.hub.teams.public.trying.note: Replaces 'Try again' on the failed-read alert while the refetch runs; the button is disabled and aria-busy. U+2026.
ui.hub.teams.public.trying.role: button label while the retry is in flight

ui.hub.teams.pull.note: The button that copies a shared team into this machine's local registry. A verb, imperative, one word; it sits at the end of a roster row. The accessible name is pull_target and must keep this word in it (label-in-name).

ui.hub.teams.pull_failed.note: The org roster's last-resort failure sentence when the pull carried no coded refusal and no message. {name} is the team's display name, quoted as English quotes it; a locale may use its own pair.
ui.hub.teams.pull_failed.role: pull-failure sentence under an org team row

ui.hub.teams.pull_target.note: Accessible name for the Pull button, naming WHICH team it pulls. {name} is the team's display name, never translated. Must contain the visible label (pull) so speech input can match what is on screen.
ui.hub.teams.pull_target.role: accessible name for the Pull control

ui.hub.teams.pulling.note: The same button while its request is in flight; every Pull on the surface is disabled while one runs, so this is a state label rather than a second action. English uses U+2026, not three periods.
